The myth likely traces to misread statements by William James about untapped potential, and possibly to the glial-cell to neuron ratio.

The myth likely came from 1950s US Army arctic experiments in which subjects' heads were the only uncovered part, and the Army manual's 40-45% figure was repeated afterward.
